HBO built its reputation on prestige television. "It's not TV, it's HBO" was not just a slogan -- for decades it was a factual statement about quality, ambition, and a willingness to go places broadcast networks would not. Then came the streaming wars, the rebrand to Max, the parent-company chaos at Warner Bros. Discovery, and a library that has become one of the most reliably progressive in premium entertainment.

We ran every HBO and Max title in the VirtueVigil database through the full VVWS dual-scoring system. The results are striking even by the standards of a platform associated with prestige and edge. HBO Max leads all premium cable and streaming platforms in average woke score across its reviewed catalog. Twelve of the fifteen titles in this list score above 5 on the woke axis. Seven of them qualify as WOKE or WOKE LEAN. Only four reach even a traditional-leaning verdict.

This is not an accident. HBO has been the primary delivery vehicle for progressive ideology in premium entertainment for the better part of a decade. The data confirms what conservative audiences already sensed. Here is every HBO and Max title VirtueVigil has reviewed, ranked from highest woke score to lowest.

  1. 1

    #1 -- Birds of Prey (2020)

    WOKE-18 WOKE

    WokeScore: 23.34 • TradScore: 5.05 • Margin: -18 WOKE

    The most woke title in the entire HBO Max catalog and one of the most agenda-forward superhero films ever produced. Birds of Prey announces its thesis in the subtitle -- "The Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn" -- and delivers on that promise without compromise. Every male character is either predatory, useless, or both. Female liberation from male control is not subtext; it is the entire plot engine. The traditional score of 5.05 is nearly the lowest in the VirtueVigil database, earned almost entirely by Margot Robbie's genuine screen presence and a handful of moments of female friendship that register as human rather than ideological. Robbie is compelling. The film knows exactly what it is selling. Conservative audiences were never the target, and the film made no attempt to pretend otherwise.

  2. 2

    #2 -- The Bride! (2026)

    WOKE-14 WOKE

    WokeScore: 22.1 • TradScore: 8.4 • Margin: -14 WOKE

    Maggie Gyllenhaal's reimagining of the Bride of Frankenstein story arrived in IMAX in 2026 and is included here as HBO-adjacent given its Warner Bros. distribution footprint. The film reframes Mary Shelley's monster mythology through an explicit feminist and queer lens: the creature's creation is framed as patriarchal violation, the Bride's awakening is framed as liberation from male ownership, and the romantic resolution refuses conventional heterosexual closure. At a woke score of 22.1, it is the second-highest score in this catalog. The trad score of 8.4 reflects some genuine tension in the narrative and the production's technical ambition. Gyllenhaal knew exactly what she was making. The monster movie genre has never been more ideologically deliberate.

  3. 3

    #3 -- The White Lotus: Season 3 (2025)

    WOKE LEAN-7 WOKE

    WokeScore: 19.5 • TradScore: 12.8 • Margin: -7 WOKE

    Mike White's third season relocated to Thailand and turned in HBO's most ideologically ambitious season yet. The Thai Buddhist setting is used not as aesthetic backdrop but as a moral counterweight to the spiritual emptiness of wealthy Western characters -- a framing that systematically positions traditional Western values as the cause of the dysfunction on screen. The critique of wealth, masculinity, and American behavior abroad is layered into every episode, and the character arcs resolve in ways that consistently punish traditional power structures. The trad score of 12.8 reflects genuine craft and the season's willingness to engage with mortality and meaning in ways that resonate regardless of ideology. White Lotus remains compelling television. It is also relentlessly progressive in its moral architecture.

  4. 4

    #4 -- Dune: Part Two (2024)

    WOKE LEAN-8 WOKE

    WokeScore: 19.36 • TradScore: 11.55 • Margin: -8 WOKE

    Denis Villeneuve's adaptation of Frank Herbert's second act is one of the most technically accomplished films of its decade and one of the most ideologically loaded blockbusters in the Max catalog. The film systematically foregrounds the danger of messianic male leadership -- a direct critique of the chosen-one mythology that Herbert embedded in the source material, but amplified here through deliberate framing choices that position Paul Atreides as a figure to be feared rather than followed. Zendaya's Chani is repositioned as the film's moral compass, her skepticism of Paul validated by the narrative in ways the novel does not support. The colonial critique is stated outright rather than embedded in subtext. Spectacular cinema that carries a progressive political argument at its structural core.

  5. 5

    #5 -- Wonder Woman 1984 (2020)

    MIXED-2 WOKE

    WokeScore: 18.18 • TradScore: 16.3 • Margin: -2 WOKE

    The most ideologically surprising entry in the HBO Max catalog. Wonder Woman 1984 lands at MIXED despite a woke score of 18.18, because its moral architecture is far more traditional than its feminist superhero packaging suggests. The film's central argument is explicitly conservative: unchecked desire destroys everything, and the only path to salvation is voluntary renunciation of what you want most. Reagan-era materialism is the villain. Every character, including Diana, must give up something precious. A father chooses his son over power. The world is saved not through force but through collective self-denial. The feminist framing and identity-forward surface push the woke score up, but the film's soul is traditional in a way that most superhero cinema is not. At -2, it is the most balanced MIXED verdict in this catalog.

  6. 6

    #6 -- Death of a Unicorn (2025)

    WOKE LEAN-5 WOKE

    WokeScore: 16.9 • TradScore: 12.3 • Margin: -5 WOKE

    This dark comedy horror film starring Paul Rudd and Jenna Ortega uses the unicorn mythology to deliver a sustained critique of pharmaceutical capitalism and elite detachment from consequence. The class critique is explicit: wealthy executives attempt to harvest a magical creature for profit and die for it, one by one. The film's progressive framework positions corporate greed as straightforwardly evil and the natural world as morally superior to human institutions. The trad score of 12.3 reflects genuine family tension between Rudd and Ortega's characters and some effective horror craft that transcends its ideological packaging. WOKE LEAN by margin, but the anti-capitalist argument is the animating force of the entire film.

  7. 7

    #7 -- Blue Beetle (2023)

    WOKE LEAN-6 WOKE

    WokeScore: 15.08 • TradScore: 8.75 • Margin: -6 WOKE

    Blue Beetle was positioned as a breakthrough for Latino superhero representation, and the film leans into that framing at every level: the Reyes family's cultural identity is foregrounded throughout, the villain is a white American defense contractor, and the film's political subtext frames corporate military power as the enemy. The family dynamics are genuinely warm and the trad score of 8.75 reflects real affection and loyalty between the Reyes family members. But the film consistently uses its identity framework as an ideological argument rather than organic character texture, and the anti-institutional messaging runs through every act. Likable characters carrying a progressive political payload.

  8. 8

    #8 -- The Matrix Resurrections (2021)

    WOKE LEAN-6 WOKE

    WokeScore: 15.05 • TradScore: 8.75 • Margin: -6 WOKE

    Lana Wachowski returned to the Matrix universe alone and made a film that is partly a sequel, partly a metacommentary on corporate franchise culture, and partly a personal statement about gender identity and the refusal to live within assigned narratives. The original Matrix was ideologically ambiguous enough that both sides of the culture war claimed it. The fourth film erases that ambiguity: the blue pill is explicitly conservative conformity, the red pill is transformation and liberation from biological and social constraint, and the film's villain is a Warner Bros. executive who forces Neo to keep making sequels. At a woke score of 15.05, this is the most explicitly ideological Matrix film, using its own mythology to make arguments the original never intended.

  9. 9

    #9 -- The Last of Us - Season 2 (2026)

    WOKE LEAN-8 WOKE

    WokeScore: 11 • TradScore: 3 • Margin: -8 WOKE

    The first season of The Last of Us was a masterpiece of prestige television that earned its emotional weight through genuine craft and character work. The second season expanded the game's most controversial storyline and in doing so produced HBO's most aggressively progressive narrative offering of 2026. The protagonist swap and the structural positioning of Ellie's rage as morally equivalent to her antagonist's is a deliberate challenge to conventional heroism. The show's treatment of Joel's legacy and the deconstruction of the protective male figure as itself a source of harm runs through every episode. A trad score of only 3 -- the lowest in this catalog -- signals how completely the show abandoned the traditional value architecture that made the first season work.

  10. 10

    #10 -- House of the Dragon (2022)

    MIXED+2 TRAD

    WokeScore: 12.92 • TradScore: 14.54 • Margin: +2 TRAD

    The Game of Thrones prequel earns a MIXED verdict by the narrowest possible margin. House of the Dragon centers on a succession crisis triggered by a female heir's claim to the Iron Throne -- a premise that carries obvious contemporary resonance and drives the progressive framing throughout. The show's sympathy lies consistently with Rhaenyra's claim and her mistreatment by a patriarchal court. But the series is also unflinching about the consequences of power, loyalty, and dynastic betrayal in ways that register as genuinely traditional. The high trad score reflects the show's respect for consequences: characters pay for their choices, alliances fracture under real pressure, and power is not romanticized. A genuinely balanced verdict on a show that never fully resolves its ideological tension.

  11. 11

    #11 -- The Flash (2023)

    MIXED+2 TRAD

    WokeScore: 9.8 • TradScore: 11.48 • Margin: +2 TRAD

    The Flash lands in MIXED territory despite the considerable weight of Ezra Miller's off-screen conduct hanging over every frame. The film itself carries modest progressive freight: the central theme -- that you cannot fix the past and must accept loss and move forward -- is genuinely traditional, and Michael Keaton's return as Bruce Wayne is the film's single best element. The woke score stays in the single digits because the film does not carry an explicit ideological agenda at the script level. The MIXED verdict reflects a movie that got the values question approximately right and the execution deeply uneven, with a third act that collapses under CGI excess and a lead whose real-world behavior made it nearly impossible for the audience to stay present. Available on Max. Worth watching for Keaton alone.

  12. 12

    #12 -- The Penguin (2024)

    TRADITIONAL LEAN+5 TRAD

    WokeScore: 9 • TradScore: 14 • Margin: +5 TRAD

    The best-scoring HBO original series in this catalog and one of the strongest arguments that prestige crime television can still operate with a traditional values framework. Colin Farrell's transformation into Oz Cobb is one of the finest performances in HBO history, and the show's crime drama structure respects consequence, loyalty, and the cost of betrayal in ways that feel genuinely earned. The woke score of 9 reflects some progressive identity framing in the supporting cast and the show's positioning of Sofia Falcone as a woman operating in a criminal patriarchy, but these elements never overwhelm the traditional crime drama architecture. Family obligation, the weight of past choices, and the inevitability of consequence -- The Penguin delivers the most traditional-leaning content in the HBO Max catalog while maintaining full prestige quality.

  13. 13

    #13 -- Space Jam: A New Legacy (2021)

    TRADITIONAL LEAN+4 TRAD

    WokeScore: 5.2 • TradScore: 8.89 • Margin: +4 TRAD

    Space Jam: A New Legacy is a film that exists primarily as an extended Warner Bros. IP showcase and secondarily as a movie for children. The woke score stays low because the film has neither the ambition nor the budget of attention required to deliver a coherent ideological message. LeBron James's relationship with his son -- a father trying to connect with a child he does not fully understand -- carries the film's only genuine emotional content and earns most of the traditional score. The IP parade is relentless and often exhausting. The values profile is clean. Conservative families watching this will find a father-son story framed with genuine warmth and very little ideological interference. Critics hated it. Kids largely did not care.

  14. 14

    #14 -- Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire (2024)

    TRADITIONAL LEAN+4 TRAD

    WokeScore: 6 • TradScore: 10 • Margin: +4 TRAD

    The fourth main-series Ghostbusters film holds a traditional lean and represents a notable course correction from the 2016 all-female reboot that became a culture war flashpoint. Frozen Empire centers the Spengler family legacy and treats intergenerational bonds -- grandmother to daughter to granddaughter -- as the film's emotional anchor. The original Ghostbusters cast's returns are handled with genuine respect. The woke score of 6 reflects some progressive casting choices in the ensemble and a few token diversity moments that carry no real ideological weight. What it does not do is weaponize the franchise against its own fanbase. After the 2016 film's deliberate alienation of legacy fans, Frozen Empire is content to be a functional franchise entry. That turns out to be enough.

    Read Full VirtueVigil Review
  15. 15

    #15 -- Mortal Kombat (2021)

    TRADITIONAL LEAN+4 TRAD

    WokeScore: 4.6 • TradScore: 8.19 • Margin: +4 TRAD

    The lowest woke score in the HBO Max catalog and the most unambiguously clean values profile in this dataset. Mortal Kombat (2021) is a brutal action film that has no interest in ideology. The story is straightforward: a man discovers his destiny, trains under pressure, and defeats evil through earned power and sacrifice. There is no feminist grievance, no systemic critique, no identity politics beyond the ensemble's diverse cast being treated as simply people who can fight. The trad score of 8.19 reflects the film's clear good-versus-evil structure, the chosen one narrative, and the father-figure relationship between Lord Raiden and his champions. Conservative action fans will find this the most comfortable title in the HBO Max library. It was made to entertain, and it does.

The HBO Max Verdict: Premium Cable's Progressive Flagship

The numbers confirm what conservative audiences have suspected for years. HBO and Max is not merely a streaming platform with some progressive content -- it is the most ideologically consistent progressive network in premium entertainment. Of the 15 titles reviewed here, only four reach a traditional-leaning verdict. Seven of them score as WOKE or WOKE LEAN. The average woke score across this catalog is 13.6, the highest of any platform in the VirtueVigil database.

That average includes some of the most technically accomplished content in modern television and film. The White Lotus is brilliant. Dune: Part Two is visually extraordinary. House of the Dragon has moments that rival anything Game of Thrones produced. HBO's progressive ideology is not a substitute for craft -- it is delivered through craft, which makes it more effective and harder to dismiss. The platform does not make bad content and call it woke. It makes excellent content and embeds a consistent progressive worldview into the structure of that content.

The bright spots exist. The Penguin is the best traditional-leaning title in the catalog and deserves a wider audience than the culture war framing around HBO generally allows it to get. Mortal Kombat is clean genre entertainment with no agenda beyond visceral action. Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire is a functional franchise entry that respects its source material and its audience. These films prove that the Warner Bros. / HBO production pipeline is capable of delivering traditionally-weighted content when it chooses to.

But the choices tell the story. Birds of Prey carries the highest woke score in this catalog and one of the highest in the VirtueVigil database. The Matrix Resurrections used a beloved franchise to deliver a personal ideological statement. The Last of Us Season 2 dismantled the moral framework that made its first season resonate with a broad audience. These are not accidents. They are a pattern.

Every title on this list has been reviewed in full at VirtueVigil with complete trope audits, creative team profiles, and parental guidance assessments.
